exposure: Folic acid supplementation regimen (consistent throughout pregnancy vs. only during early pregnancy)
cohort: The study included 416 pregnant women, with 210 consistently taking folic acid throughout pregnancy (observation group) and 206 supplementing only during early pregnancy (control group).
finding: Consistent folic acid supplementation throughout pregnancy significantly improves maternal folate status, decreases pregnancy-related complications, and enhances neonatal health outcomes, including greater newborn height, weight, head circumference, and chest circumference.
mod_finding: Consistent folic acid supplementation was associated with a reduced rate of cesarean sections (26.19% vs. 36.41%, P=0.025).
